title: Cross-frame compatibility sentinel + golden primer for streaming/tool-call/structured-output
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a cross-environment sentinel harness ('golden primer') that validates API compatibility across streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output layers. This ticket defines the regression artifacts, CI jobs, and canary gating rules needed to catch regressions introduced by runtime changes (scheduling, batching, k/v cache priming) as well as model shim behavior. The harness should: 1) execute a curated golden prompt matrix that exercises interleaved streaming and tool calls; 2) assert structured-output schemas and fallback NDJSON framing; 3) fingerprint output behavior to detect subtle protocol drift; 4) run deterministically in CI with seeded stochasticity and a failure classification tiering (hard fail vs flaky warning).
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic golden prompt corpus (>=40 prompts) that covers: simple toolcall, nested function call sequences, partial-JSON fragments, streaming chunk boundaries, and KV-cache priming scenarios
Automated validator that checks streamed chunk sequencing, tool-call invocation ordering, and final structured-output JSON schema conformance with schema versioning tags
CI jobs added to gitlab/github actions: nightly-full (expensive), pre-merge-smoke (fast), and post-deploy-canary (targeted); pre-merge-smoke must run in <6 minutes
Fingerprinting metric implemented (checksum+behavioral-hash) and dashboarded with alert thresholds; regressions triaged with automated flakiness classification
Failure modes documented with remediation playbook and at least two approved runbooks linked
Compatibility sentinel produces actionable diffs and links to failing PRs/commits when run in CI canary
test_plan: Stage 1: author golden corpus and canonical expected outputs for current runtime-1.20; store seeds and deterministic model-stub responses in fixtures/
Stage 2: implement stream-frame validator that replays NDJSON chunks and asserts order, framing, and incremental tool invocation tokens
Stage 3: JSON-schema checker with schema-version header acceptance and structured output fallback validators (ndjson -> schema)
Stage 4: integrate fingerprinting and flakiness classifier using historical CI runs; tune thresholds to <=2% false positives on known-good baseline
Stage 5: wire into CI: pre-merge-smoke on PRs touching runtime, nightly-full on main, canary-run on deploy to staging and dedicated pools
decisions: Use a seeded model-stub for pre-merge-smoke to keep run-time under 6 minutes; nightly/full runs will use sampled real model variants
Fingerprint = SHA256 over normalized token stream + canonicalized tool-call metadata; store both raw and canonical hashes for debugging
Treat structured-output schema mismatches as P0 regressions; treat minor chunk timing jitter as flakiness unless it results in out-of-order toolcalls
Prefer NDJSON framing checks over full-string equality to allow benign whitespace/escape differences while catching structural breakages
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created. Initial scoping and corpus sketch uploaded to Confluence (see links). Assigned to Marco for implementation. Aisha to own corpus curation.

2026-03-11: Prototype stream-frame validator landed in branch eng/compat/sentinel-proto. It replays stored NDJSON artifacts and asserts chunk sequence numbers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1827

2026-03-12: Discussion with QA and Platform — decided to seed a lightweight model-stub for fast smoke runs. Trade-off: slightly less fidelity vs. faster feedback. QA OK with nightly real-model sampling.

2026-03-13: Reviewed by runtime team @design-review. Feedback: make schema version header explicit in responses; ensure validator tolerates legacy schema v1 fallbacks. Action: add schema-version header parsing to validator.

2026-03-14: CI integration spike successful on staging; pre-merge-smoke job created in .github/workflows/compat-smoke.yml. Initial flakiness observed on two prompts that exercise interleaved tool preemption — adding to flaky-exempt list pending deeper fix (ENG-24686 created).
flakiness_mitigation: Seed all randomness and persist seeds with each CI run to allow deterministic replays
Tier failures: hard-fail if schema mismatch or tool-call reordering; convert ephemeral timing issues to flakes and surface in PR comment with repro command
Maintain separate golden corpus subsets: smoke (fast, deterministic), extended (nightly), and model-matrix (weekly across variants)
Automated rerun-once for transient network/server errors before marking as failed
next_steps: Finish golden corpus (Aisha) and land fixtures into runtime/testdata/golden/
Address flaky prompts in ENG-24686 and re-evaluate fingerprint thresholds
Complete PR review for stream-frame validator and add schema-header parsing (Marco)
Add canary gating rule in deployment pipeline to block runtime rollout on P0 sentinel failures
